backlog.spec: Extend featurize() so each molecule's row also contains: the 167 MACCS keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys converted to a numpy array), an atom-pair count fingerprint of 1024 bins (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator(fpSize=1024).GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy) and a topological-torsion count fingerprint of 1024 bins (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetTopologicalTorsionGenerator(fpSize=1024).GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy). Concatenate them after the existing Morgan bits and descriptors, as float32. Build the generators once per featurize() call, not once per molecule. Leave the models and the rank-average blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Add MACCS keys and RDKit atom-pair / topological-torsion count fingerprints

backlog.spec: Fit a third model, an LGBMClassifier (n_estimators=400, learning_rate=0.05, num_leaves=15, colsample_bytree=0.6, min_child_samples=20, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8, verbose=-1), on the descriptor columns alone, that is the 11 physchem features plus the clipped full descList block with no Morgan bits, and return 0.4 * scaled_rank(rf) + 0.4 * scaled_rank(gb_full) + 0.2 * scaled_rank(gb_desc). Rationale: descriptors are what produced every accepted gain, but in the full matrix they compete with 2048 sparse bits for column subsampling, so a member that cannot see the fingerprint is forced to model physicochemistry only; because blood-brain-barrier penetration is largely driven by size, lipophilicity and polarity, this member should generalize across unseen scaffolds and decorrelate the two fingerprint-aware members.
backlog.title: Add a descriptor-only LightGBM as a third blend member

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, after building X_train and X_test, compute a column mask from X_train only: remove columns that are constant, and remove Morgan-bit columns (the first N_BITS columns) that are non-zero in fewer than 3 training molecules. Apply the same mask to X_test. Then fit the RF and LightGBM as now. This removes noise columns that waste the per-split feature sampling (max_features=0.3, colsample_bytree=0.3).
backlog.title: Drop constant and near-duplicate features before fitting

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, fit the RandomForest and the LGBMClassifier three times each with random_state = seed, seed + 1, seed + 2 (all other hyperparameters unchanged), average the three predicted probability vectors within each family, then rank-scale each family average and combine the two with the existing equal weights. Keep n_jobs as they are and, if runtime is a concern, drop RF n_estimators to 200 per seed so total tree count is similar. Rationale: a large part of the run-to-run spread noted for the incumbent is estimator-level randomness (bootstrap draws, feature subsampling, LightGBM tie-breaking), and seed averaging reduces that variance at no bias cost, which should both lower the mean loss slightly and make future deltas easier to read.
backlog.title: Average three seeds per blend member

backlog.spec: The dataset is imbalanced (most molecules are class 1). Pass class_weight='balanced_subsample' to RandomForestClassifier and class_weight='balanced' to LGBMClassifier. Change nothing else. The output is rank-averaged, so calibration shift does not matter; the aim is better ranking of the minority class.
backlog.title: Balanced class weights in both models

backlog.spec: Replace the single LightGBM fit with 5 fits that differ only in random_state (seed, seed+1, ..., seed+4), each with subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1 added to the current settings so that the seeds actually produce different models. Average the 5 class-1 probability vectors, then apply scaled_rank to that average and blend 50/50 with scaled_rank of the RF predictions as now.
backlog.title: Seed-bag the LightGBM member

backlog.spec: Add a linear third model to the blend. Build its input from the same X_train/X_test: standardize the non-fingerprint columns (everything after the first N_BITS columns) with sklearn StandardScaler fitted on the training rows after applying np.sign(x)*np.log1p(np.abs(x)) to them; leave the Morgan bit columns as 0/1. Fit sklearn.linear_model.LogisticRegression(C=0.05, penalty='l2', solver='lbfgs', max_iter=2000, random_state=seed). Return the weighted mean of scaled ranks: 0.4 RF + 0.4 LightGBM + 0.2 logistic regression.
backlog.title: Add a scaled logistic-regression member on descriptors plus fingerprints

backlog.spec: After building X_train and X_test in fit_predict but before fitting, compute the column-wise count of nonzero entries over the Morgan bit block of X_train only and keep only bits set in at least 5 training molecules; apply the same boolean mask to the test matrix. Leave the 11 physchem columns and the clipped descList columns always kept, and implement the mask with a single numpy boolean index so the code stays short. Rationale: most of the 2048 bits fire in a handful of molecules, carry almost no generalizable signal across unseen Murcko scaffolds, and act as noise draws in both the forest's feature subsampling and LightGBM's colsample_bytree; removing them raises the informative fraction of every candidate split set without touching the descriptor signal that drives the current gain.
backlog.title: Drop rare fingerprint bits inside each fold

backlog.spec: Change only the LGBMClassifier settings in fit_predict to n_estimators=800, learning_rate=0.02, num_leaves=31, min_child_samples=20, colsample_bytree=0.15, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, keeping random_state=seed, n_jobs=8, verbose=-1. The RandomForest, the features and the equal-weight rank average stay as they are. Rationale: earlier LightGBM experiments changed the boosting algorithm (DART, lgb.train, extra_trees, monotone constraints) rather than the basic capacity/shrinkage trade-off, and the current member is a fairly fast, shallow fit; with a wide mixed sparse-plus-dense matrix a smaller learning rate with many more rounds, row subsampling for variance reduction, and a thinner column fraction is the standard setting that extracts more from dense descriptor columns. Check the job still fits the 10-minute limit; if not, cut n_estimators to 600.
backlog.title: Retuned LightGBM member: slower, deeper, thinner columns

backlog.spec: Change N_BITS from 2048 to 512 (keep RADIUS = 2) so the Morgan hashed-bit block is a quarter of its current width while the 11 physchem descriptors and the full clipped descList block are unchanged. Nothing else in fit_predict changes. Rationale: the recorded gains all came from descriptors, and with only ~1300 training molecules per fold a 2048-bit sparse block mostly contributes near-constant, scaffold-specific columns that dilute the column subsampling of both the forest (max_features=0.3) and LightGBM (colsample_bytree=0.3); a narrower, denser-on-average fingerprint should raise the chance that each split candidate is informative and should also cut runtime.
backlog.title: Shrink the Morgan block to 512 bits

memo: Helped: the RF+LightGBM blend (0.1194 vs baseline ~0.1361) and appending RDKit descriptors (11 physchem 0.1040; full descList 0.0944 and 0.0842, incumbent mean_adjusted 0.0893 over 2 runs). Descriptors drive the gain. Did not help: other fingerprint swaps or additions (atom-pair 0.0949, MACCS 0.0921, Morgan counts 0.0940, BRICS 0.0938), model swaps (XGBoost 0.1041, CatBoost 0.0950, ExtraTrees 0.0948, SVC 0.1255), LightGBM variants (DART 0.0967, regularized 0.0958, monotone 0.0942), and extra members like LR or MLP. Tanimoto kNN (0.0884), label spreading (0.0896), torsion counts (0.0902) and LR stacking (0.0900) were within noise. The two incumbent runs differ by about 0.01, twice the noise sd of ~0.0049, so single-run deltas under 0.01 are unreliable. Next: replicate the incumbent and the kNN variant to firm up the baseline. Tune blend weights and tree hyperparameters on the descriptors. Try fewer fingerprint bits. Avoid more fingerprint swaps, kernel models and model-family swaps.
